title: Personal Checking: Bank-Side Postings and Balance-Based Fee Determinations
content:
## Scope

This page explains, for Personal Checking, how the bank's own postings on an account relate to a fee determination that is decided on the account's close-of-business balance. The determination it concerns is the same-day review of a monthly maintenance fee dated the cycle closing date, raised by the owner of an active account, in which the tier's relationship waiver is decided on that day's close-of-business balance. The page concerns that review on an account which the bank, at the same time, owes credits of the kinds Personal Checking treats as owed: refunds of fees charged contrary to the charter, and provisional credits that have fallen due on submitted disputes.

A matter of this kind is settled once three things hold together: what the bank owed now stands on the ledger, the relationship waiver has been decided for the fee in question on the balance at that day's close of business, and the fee has come back as a bank-error refund if the waiver turned out to be met.

## Who makes these postings

A refund the bank owes, a provisional credit that has fallen due, and the refund that a waiver review decides are all entries the bank makes on its own side. None of them is an owner's consent or an owner's claim under the Personal Checking terms, so none of them is for the customer to carry out; the agent books each of them.

## How the postings bear on a balance-based determination

Each such posting lifts the ledger balance kept on the account record. The entry it creates carries nothing the determination reads; the determination looks only at the ledger balance, so the postings reach it solely through the balance they leave behind.

Owed credits stand apart from one another. Every one is booked as its own entry, for its own sum, against the entry it answers, and none takes any figure from another. Adding the same sums to a ledger lands on the same total whichever of them goes on the books ahead of the rest, so the sequence among them changes no amount and no decision.

A bank-side posting is complete at the moment it is booked. Its effect on the ledger does not depend on any outside event or on the passing of time.
